name: Pendon
comment: Pendon grammar for .mdp files. The normative syntax is docs/spec/SYNTAX.md; this file only encodes what that document describes and delegates every construct Pendon does not override to VS Code's built-in text.html.markdown grammar. The Pendon rules come first so they win over the Markdown ones.

block.comment: Block dispatch: Pendon rules first, then the built-in Markdown rules, then the paragraph.

pendon.comment: Every Pendon rule. The injection grammar (syntaxes/pendon-injection.tmLanguage.json) includes this one, so .md files get Pendon highlighting too.

pendonBlock.comment: Block-level Pendon constructs; the most specific sigil is listed first.

inlinePendon.comment: Inline Pendon constructs, most specific sigil first: the `@@` heads, the numbering marker, then the tagged slot heads (cite, wiki, anchor, image), the marker, the directive and finally the Markdown link.

paragraph.comment: A copy of text.html.markdown#paragraph with the Pendon inline rules in front (the built-in rule can only be reached through #block, which never sees them).
paragraph.name: meta.paragraph.pendon

inlineContent.comment: Inline content of a heading, table caption or marker: Pendon rules first, then the built-in Markdown inline rules.

bracketContents.comment: §5.2 — the three contents of a bracket, plus the modifier run (§5.4) that can end it.

parenContents.comment: §5.2 — the three contents of a paren. A paren carries no modifier run, so `|` is ordinary content here.

citeContents.comment: §5.2/§7.3 — a citation's bracket: the same three contents, with the bare one read as the reference.

slotModifier.comment: §5.4 — the modifier run. `|` opens it only at the start of a word (the head or a space) and everything after it up to the `]` is a symbol — `\` included, which is not an escape there.
slotModifier.name: meta.slot.modifier.pendon

slotTick.comment: §5.2 — the tick content, `` `x` ``. Like the parser, a delimiter closes only at a boundary, so `"q"`t`` is one quote content and not a quote plus a tick.
slotTick.name: string.other.slot.tick.pendon

slotQuoteDouble.comment: §5.2 — the quote content, `"x"`; §6.1 decides what the position means.
slotQuoteDouble.name: string.quoted.double.slot.pendon

slotQuoteSingle.comment: §5.2 — the single-quoted spelling of the quote content, `'x'`.
slotQuoteSingle.name: string.quoted.single.slot.pendon

slotBare.comment: §5.2 — the bare content: whatever a delimiter did not claim. It may contain spaces, so this is the last rule of a slot.
slotBare.name: string.unquoted.slot.bare.pendon

slotGroup.comment: §5.2 — a slot pair: the bracket and the paren attached to it (§4.1). Untagged, so only a head something else already claimed (`{{type}}`, `@@type`, a directive) may carry one (§5.3).

headGroups.comment: §5.2/§5.3 — the slot pair of a head with no `{…}` body. It is untagged because the `@@` sigil already claimed it.
headGroups.name: meta.head.pendon

headTypedBody.comment: §5 — `@@type[slug]("title"){…}`. The body must be adjacent and closed on the same line; an unterminated head is stopped at the line end (compare §4.3).
headTypedBody.name: meta.head.pendon

headBare.comment: §4.1 — an untyped `{…}` head must touch the construct it decorates. A `{` that follows whitespace or opens the line is literal text.
headBare.name: meta.head.pendon

numberMark.comment: §5/§10.5 — the `%%numberType` numbering marker: a `%` run of 2..7, then a name. A single `%`, a run of 8+ and `%%` with no name stay literal text (D-9), so the run is bounded on both sides.
numberMark.name: meta.number-mark.pendon

headTypeOnly.comment: §4.4 — a typed head with neither groups nor body. A type followed by whitespace and a body is literal text, so nothing is claimed here (§4.3).
headTypeOnly.name: meta.head.type-only.pendon

marker.comment: §6.1 — a `{{type}}` marker; its groups (and any head) must follow the closing braces immediately.
marker.name: meta.marker.pendon

markerGroups.comment: §6.1 — the slot pair of a marker; it must touch the `}}`.
markerGroups.name: meta.marker.pendon

citeReference.comment: §7.3 — the citation's bare content is its reference, not a generic position, so it keeps the reference scope.
citeReference.name: variable.other.reference.cite.pendon

citation.comment: §7.3 — `[^reference_id "locator"](…)`: `^` sits inside the bracket and is the tag. The bare content is the reference, the quoted one the locator; the paren and the tick are preset-less positions, so they stay fields (D-7).
citation.name: meta.citation.pendon

anchor.comment: §7.2 — `@[inner text](href "title")`: the `@` tag claims the bracket and the paren attached to it. Without the tag the text is a Markdown link and an adjacent head stays literal (§14).
anchor.name: meta.anchor.pendon

image.comment: §7.1 — `![alt](src)`: `!` is the tag, so the bracket and the paren are the whole head and the alt may be empty. The retired `!!` / `?~w300` marker run is ordinary text now (§14).
image.name: meta.image.pendon

valueItems.comment: §5 — the items of a nested `{…}` object or `[…]` array. `specs.*`, `.class`, `#id` and the tick do not exist inside a value, so the specs rules are not offered here.

wiki.comment: §7.5 — `[[Target | Label]]`: the label is split off the first `|` (both sides are trimmed) and an empty target stays literal text. A wikilink's content is never re-interpreted, so the target and the label are single scopes.
wiki.name: meta.wikilink.pendon

inlineDirective.comment: §10.2 — `::type[…]("…") content ::`: the content is inline content and the closing run must be at least as long as the opening one. `\1` is the opening run, so a longer close is accepted, a run followed by a letter opens a nested directive instead of closing this one, and a run that no closer ever follows (an unterminated opener, §4.3) never opens at all; `(^)` is the safety net for a region whose closer the scan missed.
inlineDirective.name: meta.directive.inline.pendon

link.comment: §7.2 — a Markdown inline link. Pendon does not claim it: without the `@` tag there is no anchor and the URL modifiers are gone (§14), so `^`, `!`, `$`, `;;` and `--` are ordinary URL characters. URLs may nest parentheses two levels deep.
link.name: meta.link.pendon

headings.comment: §7.4 — ATX headings with Pendon heads: the groups are adjacent to the `#` run and the extras may follow the title. One rule per level (`$1` in `name` substitutes matched text, not a count).

heading1.comment: §7.4 — `#` heading. A claimed head spends one `#` on the tag (D-11), so capture 2 is the slot pair of a depth-(run − 1) heading and capture 3 the title with its Pendon heads.
heading1.name: markup.heading.1.pendon

decorator.comment: §9.1/D-10 — a decorator line: `@@`, then type → slot pair → `{specs}` → `%%numbering`, in that order. `@@` is mandatory (a bare `{…}` line is literal text, §14) and a body nests two levels deep.
decorator.name: meta.decorator.pendon

headItems.comment: §5 — the items of a head body; §19 adds the `$ref` and `...spread` forms. Anything not recognised stays literal text.

itemEscape.comment: §5 — `\` escapes the next character of a value.
itemEscape.name: constant.character.escape.pendon

itemSpread.comment: §19 — `...$ref` spreads a bind path into the head.
itemSpread.name: meta.spread.head.pendon

itemRef.comment: §19 — a `$name` reference to a bind path, with `.property`, `[0]` and `["key"]` steps.

itemString.comment: §5 — a double-quoted value. The closing quote must be on the same line, so an unterminated value stays literal text.
itemString.name: string.quoted.double.pendon

itemCustomProperty.comment: §6.1 — `--name: value` fills `specs.style`; the `::` form cannot be used inside a head body because `::` opens an inline directive.
itemCustomProperty.name: meta.specs.style.pendon

itemClass.name: meta.specs.class.pendon
itemClass.comment: §6.1 — `.x` fills `specs.class` (a `class:` prop joins it exactly like a `.x` item).

itemKey.comment: §5 — `key: value`; `::` is an inline directive, never a key/value separator.

itemBare.comment: §5 — anything else is a bare value (including flags, which are values too).
itemBare.name: string.unquoted.pendon

sectionDeepen.comment: §9.5 — a line whose trimmed content is exactly `<--->` deepens the outline by one section.
sectionDeepen.name: meta.section.deepen.pendon

sectionClose.comment: §9.5 — a line whose trimmed content is exactly `>---<` closes the innermost section (a Markdown blockquote elsewhere).
sectionClose.name: meta.section.close.pendon

tableCaption.comment: §8 — a `||…||` caption line, before the rows.
tableCaption.name: meta.table.caption.pendon

tableFoot.comment: §8 — the `|===|` foot separator line (bare `===` is retired).
tableFoot.name: meta.table.foot.pendon

headExtras.comment: §5 — the shared extras head on its own, for slots where nothing else may be interpreted (a decorator line, a childless table declaration).

table.comment: §8 — the body rows, shaped like text.html.markdown#table: the first row opens the region, the rest continue it, and a non-row line ends it.
table.name: meta.table.body.pendon

tableWidth.comment: §8 — a width token `(200px)`, directly after the alignment code (or the opening `|`).

tableSpan.comment: §8 — the `>` (colspan) / `^` (rowspan) markers, which come before the cell head.

tableCell.comment: §8 — a cell's content, up to the next `|`; `\|` escapes a pipe inside it.

tableExtras.comment: §8 — a table slot: the extras head first (a cell head touches its `|`), then the inline rules.

blockDirective.comment: §10.3 — `==type … ==`. The body is block content, so directives nest; a fence alone on a line closes the innermost open directive.
blockDirective.name: meta.directive.block.pendon

bindBlock.comment: §19 — data blocks. A block starts at the beginning of a line; a head that carries no payload must be alone on its line.

bindFile.comment: §19 — file payload: `{{{csv[rows](../data/rows.csv)}}}`, closed on the same line.
bindFile.name: meta.bind.block.pendon

bindBodyToml.comment: §19 — `toml` body. VS Code ships no TOML grammar, so `source.toml` resolves only when the user has one installed.
bindBodyToml.name: meta.bind.block.pendon

bindBodyCsv.comment: §19 — `csv` body; no CSV grammar is bundled, so the payload fields are scoped here (comma, quoted / numeric / boolean / unquoted field).
bindBodyCsv.name: meta.bind.block.pendon

bindBodyMdp.comment: §19 — `mdp` body: specified but not implemented (the pipeline warns and drops the block), so the payload is not tokenized as Pendon.
bindBodyMdp.name: meta.bind.block.pendon

mathInline.comment: plugin-latex — inline math `$…$`. Mirrors the plugin scanner: `\$` is a literal dollar, a `$` touching a space neither opens nor closes, and an unclosed `$` (e.g. `$100`) stays literal.
mathInline.name: meta.math.inline.pendon

mathDisplay.comment: plugin-latex — display math `$$…$$` on one line. `\$` escapes; a lone interior `$` is part of the formula, `$$` closes it.
mathDisplay.name: meta.math.display.pendon
